<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

b.cafe880ee3:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>C</c>allístus, Románus, prǽfuit Ecclésiæ, Antoníno Heliogábalo imperatóre. Constítuit quátuor anni Témpora, quibus ieiúnium, ex apostólica traditióne accéptum, ab ómnibus servarétur. Ædificávit basílicam sanctæ Maríæ trans Tíberim, et in via Appia vetus cœmetérium ampliávit, in quo multi sancti Sacerdótes et Mártyres sepúlti sunt; unde ab eo Callísti cœmetérium appellátur. Sedit annos quinque, mensem unum, dies duódecim. Post longam famem crebrásque verberatiónes præceps iactus in púteum, martýrio coronátus sub Alexándro imperatóre, et sepúltus est in cœmetério Calepódii, via Aurélia, tértio ab Urbe lápide, prídie idus octóbris. Eius póstmodum corpus in basílicam sanctæ Maríæ trans Tíberim delátum, sub ara maióri, máxima veneratióne cólitur.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>allistus, a Roman, was head of the Church while Antonius Heliogabalus was emperor. He fixed the four periods of the year for the Ember days, on which the custom of fasting, handed down by tradition from the Apostolic times, was to be observed by all. He built the Basilica of St. Mary across the Tiber. Because he enlarged the old cemetery on the Appian Way, where many holy priests and martyrs were buried, it is now called the cemetery of St. Callistus. He reigned for five years one month and twelve days. After long starvation and many scourging he was thrown headforemost into a well, and so won the crown of martyrdom under the emperor Alexander. His body was buried in the cemetery of Calepodius in the Aurelian Way at the third milestone from the city, on October 14. Later it was placed under the high altar of the Basilica of St. Mary across the Tiber, where it is venerated with great honor.

b.3b7e23b435:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 15th 2027, the 15th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Avila, in Spain, the holy Virgin Theresa, the mother and mistress of the brethren and sisters of the Order of Carmelites of the Stricter Observance.
<h>A</h>t Cracow, in Poland, the birthday of the holy widow Iadwiga, Grand Princess of the Poles, who gave herself up to the serving of the poor, and was famous ever for miracles. The Supreme Pontiff Clement IV enrolled her name among those of the Saints; but her feast is kept upon the morrow.
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Fortunatus.
<h>I</h>n Prussia, (at the beginning of the eleventh century,) the holy martyr Bruno, Bishop of the Ruthenians, who was preaching the gospel in those parts when he was taken by wicked men, who cut off, first his hands and feet, and then his head.
<h>A</h>t Cologne, three hundred holy martyrs, who finished the course of their contending in the persecution under Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Carthage, the holy martyr Agileus, on whose feast - day holy Augustine preached to the people a discourse concerning him.
<h>A</h>t Lyon, (in the fourth century,) holy Antiochus, Bishop (of that see,) who vigorously administered the office of the bishopric to which he had been called, and inherited a kingdom in heaven.
<h>A</h>t Trier, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Severus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Strasbourg, (in the year 1027,) the holy Virgin Aurelia.
<h>I</h>n Germany, (in the eighth century,) holy Thecla, Abbess (of Kitzingen.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
